svg.title: Restricted spectral equivalence and the full Hecke-lisse image
svg.desc: A finite residue-cotangent calculation makes the full framed Betti algebra bounded. Arbitrary categorical targets identify its framed and unframed Betti categories. The supported complement is generated by outside residue fields. A nonzero categorical residue field detects the original ind-connection counit, forcing the coefficient functor to kill that complement. Conservative frames give the actual restricted spectral equivalence, its unital action and the full Hecke-lisse image. Nilpotent singular support and original-field regularity remain separate geometric criteria.
svg.text: The actual restricted spectral equivalence and its geometric image
Connected reductive H over C; every complex curve genus; full unbounded categories.
1. Closed-point cotangent fibres give a bounded Betti ambient — RSE.1–RSE.14
Y(Betti) = Spec B; L(B) perfect; every closed C-point is restricted.
Residue cotangent amplitude [−1,0] ⇒ local finite Koszul algebras P[ε₁,…,εᵣ].
A finite cover bounds the exterior lengths: Hʲ(B)=0 outside [−N,0].
L = Fun(K,Mod(C)) is dualizable; I ↪ L has a continuous right adjoint g∞.
The original ind-connection category I is retained; its completion is not substituted.
2. Arbitrary categorical targets identify the full Betti comparison — RSE.15–RSE.24
Frame the regular algebra: C ≃ (Mod(S,C))ᴴ, with the whole algebraic nerve.
For every T, put D = End(T)(1); framed tensor functors = Y(Betti)(τ≤⁰D).
R(L), framed ≃ Mod(B) ⇒ R(L) ≃ A(Betti) = Mod(B)ᴴ.
Unit endomorphisms, free-module bars and Hopf coordinates give all maps and paths.
The equivalence is the actual universal-coefficient map, including changes of frame.
3. The supported complement has all-prime residue generators — RSE.25–RSE.27
S = union of the closed coefficient loci in Spec H⁰(B).
Γ(S) = C(S) ⊗ᴸ(B) −; Q(S) = cofib(Γ(S) → id).
Bounded B has a finite filtration by its H⁰(B)-module cohomology layers.
Tensor that finite filtration with any unbounded M; then apply residue generation.
ker Γ(S) = Loc{ k(p) : p outside S }, including generic residue fields.
4. A nonzero categorical field detects the ind-connection counit — RSE.28–RSE.35
Suppose Φ(k(p)) ≠ 0. T(p) = Mod(Φ(k(p)),T) has nonzero unit.
Mod(k(p)) → T(p) is conservative; so is its tensor extension by L.
Coefficients of Φ in T ⊗ I ⇒ the actual point p has coefficients in Mod(k(p)) ⊗ I.
Thus p lies in S. For p outside S, Φ(k(p))=0 ⇒ Φ kills ker Γ(S).
Conservative regular frames and the full functor-space comparison give
L(I) : R(I) ≃ A = QCoh(Z restricted), with L(I) Q(Ran) = L(r).
5. Transported action and the exact full geometric image — RSE.36–RSE.38
The full Hecke-lisse category N carries a continuous unital A-action Ψ.
The actual geometric idempotent Π sends every automorphic object into N.
Π restricted to N = Ψ(L(r)p,−) ≃ Ψ(1,−) ≃ id(N).
Therefore EssIm(Π) = N as a full DG subcategory, on all unbounded objects.
A unit or adjunction for p is not inferred from its nonunital idempotent algebra.
6. Three sharp tests and the remaining geometric scope — RSE.39–RSE.47
C[t,t⁻¹]: every closed character is restricted; the generic character is not.
C(S) = fib(R → C(t)); H¹(C(S)) = C(t)/R; ker Γ(S)=Loc{C(t)}.
Bounded odd exterior algebras allow arbitrary unbounded modules.
For C[z], |z|=−2, the nonzero localization C[z,z⁻¹] has zero classical fibre.
Nilpotent singular support and original-field ind-regularity need their geometric criteria.
The spectral and Hecke-lisse conclusions above do not assert those extra criteria.
Exact proofs: §§3.217–3.231, RSE.1–RSE.47; Solutions3.DP–3.DR.
Spectral framework: AGKRRV, arXiv:2010.01906v2; all comparison proofs are local.
